item.title: The graphics in GTA 6 are so realistic that actual photos and videos are being mistaken as screenshots or clips from the game.
item.description:
The graphics in GTA 6 are so realistic that actual photos and videos are being mistaken as screenshots or clips from the game.
It feels like every social media platform is chock-full of posts about Rockstar’s latest release, which has cemented itself as the biggest entertainment launch of all time. Everybody’s talking about it; it’s practically impossible to scroll through your timeline without seeing it in some form or another.
GTA 6 is a good-looking game, to say the least, with some of the most realistic visuals we’ve seen in a digital world thus far — to the point where it’s genuinely hard to tell the difference between what’s from the game and what’s from real life.
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
For instance, a video taken from influencer India Love’s live stream sparked a swath of comments from viewers who had to do a double-take to make sure they weren’t watching a clip from GTA 6, partly owing to the lighting. If anything, that just goes to show how realistic the game’s lighting really is, with one user writing on Twitter/X, “Why is everything lit so well in that game? How did they do that?”
gta6 has pan seared my brain
“I was confused by your post because I didn't know what part of the game this is,” another commented, while another admitted that they “haven’t even played GTA 6 and I thought it was a clip from it at first.”
Another person posted photos of a shirtless Jack Donoghue posing in a speedboat at sea, prompting no end of comments mistaking him for someone’s Jason in the game.
“Close enough, welcome back Jason Duval,” one joked, while another remarked, “Why did I think that this was Jason from GTA for a second?”
@Charismah411 Why did I think that this was Jason from gta for a second
Someone else posted photos of their dog that they took on 35mm film, showing the fluffy pup playing on a basketball court — and once again, players couldn’t help but admit that they’d accidentally mistaken the pictures for GTA 6 screenshots.
“Everything is a GTA 6 screenshot now. I'm cooked,” one user said.
“Lowkey thought this was GTA 6, my brain is done,” another added.
Everything is a GTA 6 screenshot now. I'm cooked.
However, it’s likely that this trend isn’t solely due to GTA 6’s fantastic graphics; if you’re totally absorbed in something over a long enough period of time, you’re more likely to see patterns from that thing in other areas of your life. In other words, yes, GTA 6’s graphics are out of this world — but also, it’s impossible to get away from this game right now, and if you’re playing it, you’ve probably got ‘GTA 6 brain.’

item.title: GTA 6 is receiving praise for its commentary on how hard it is for felons to start a life and the system that breeds crime.
item.description:
GTA 6 is receiving praise for its commentary on how hard it is for felons to start a new life and the system that breeds crime.
In GTA 6, Jason and Lucia choose a life of crime in hopes of creating financial stability in their lives. Their goal isn't necessarily to get rich and buy flashy cars or a mansion, but so they can lay the foundation for their family. Although Jason runs drugs for a local crime boss, Lucia in particular is the one who really pushes them to take on more ambitious jobs. Some players felt that her decision-making at the start of the game was a bit reckless, given that she just got out of prison — but if you read her text messages, things begin to make a lot more sense.
Players realized that her parole officer had denied her petition to take a job at a local bar, one of her only options for employment because she knew someone who worked there that could vouch for her. Without that, her record as a convicted felon would make it difficult for employers to consider her for a position. Her PO also noted that she's overdue on paying court-ordered parole fees, which she can't pay because she doesn't have a job, putting her in a vicious cycle.
Lucia's willingness to get back into crime makes a lot more sense when you look at her texts with her PO and see that they denied her request to get a job but still wanted her to pay bills she has no money for https://t.co/HBfpsZEmz2
This pushes Lucia to get involved with shady characters who turn her life with Jason upside down. A number of fans have praised this particular narrative beat, including some who have worked within this very system.
"As someone who worked as part of the system years ago, not as a PO but a case manager, this is wildly accurate to real life," said X user Mgs2master. "Rockstar did their homework here."
"GTA 6 is brave enough to try and educate the player on how desperation can drive you to crime through how it incorporates gameplay mechanics into the story," said one player. "It's genuinely one of the best uses of ludonarrative I’ve ever seen, period. I am floored."
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
"As someone who's had family that has had to go through this s**t, it's genuinely not satirical," said another user. "This is straight up just what happens. The system is designed to funnel criminals back into crime by denying them opportunities needed to rehabilitate themselves to keep prisons full."
Another person noted that this system blocks people out of having a reasonable chance of developing a good life: "The US has a recidivism problem because once you have a felony you're essentially locked out of a good chunk of employment and housing stuff, and then these orgs act surprised when people go back to crime. The econ equivalent of kicking people while they're down."
Rockstar Games writer Rupert Humphries told Love Magazine earlier this year that the "American Dream" as we know it has scaled down for many people with each passing GTA game. Now, people just want a foundation to live and build a family, but the state of the world has made that increasingly unattainable, and in the case of GTA 6, it leads to the characters taking matters into their own hands.
Jason and Lucia Screenshots
"Some would say the American Dream collapsed a long time ago," said Humphries. "With GTA 4, we told an immigrant’s story that was supposed to be a kind of hollow commentary on the illusion of America as a land of opportunity, and then we sort of doubled down on that with the cynicism of GTA 5. Maybe the American Dream is more modest now. It’s a house for your family and your loans paid off instead of wild success — but maybe today, that is just as out of reach for the average person. Miami and Southern Florida are a particular front line for this battle between astronomical wealth and unbounded ambition, creating a pressure cooker for all kinds of insanity."
Of course, GTA 6 is still fiction and isn't an endorsement of real crime, despite how much some people would like you to believe otherwise. It's more so putting two charcaters in these circumstances and seeing how they react to the cards they're dealt. There also wouldn't be much of a game if Lucia decided to just spend the rest of her days scrounging for minimum wage work, after all.
GTA 6 has been a roaring success so far, generating over $3.79 billion in revenue in its first 24 hours with over 32.5 million copies sold in pre-sales alone. The game is also a critical smash hit, tying with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the best reviewed video game in history on Metacritic. IGN gave GTA 6 a 10 out of 10, praising it for its depth and detail.

item.title: GTA 5's unstoppable train has been a meme for a decade, so naturally, players wasted no time trying to stop GTA 6's train – but they were sad to find out that it wasn't all that hard to do.
item.description:
GTA 5's unstoppable train has been a meme for a decade, so naturally, players wasted no time trying to stop the one in GTA 6 – but they were sad to find out that it wasn't all that hard to do.
What better way to spend the early days of a project that Rockstar Games fans waited 13 years for than to immediately do the same thing they've already been doing? As players were dropped into the south end of Leonida, many immediately took Jason as far as they could just to find a train to stand in front of.
There is, indeed, a new train screeching over the tracks surrounding Vice City, but there's a problem – it has no aura.
Finally, the train in GTA 6 has come to stop 😭😭😭😭 https://t.co/ly0JOJ0Mb0
So sánh tàu hỏa đối đầu với các phương tiện trong GTA5 vs GTA6 vs PDR2 https://t.co/M4CwCbgokx
If you're one of the few people who hasn't picked up GTA 5 since it launched in 2013, you still may have heard about its unstoppable train. The iconic black, yellow, and white locomotive patrols Los Santos and has for years, and unlike just about every other vehicle in the game, there's nothing Michael, Franklin, or Trevor can do to stop it.
Dumb trucks, C4, planes, rows of cars – you name it. No one has ever been able to get GTA 5's train to budge. After 13 years of trying, it's become a meme on the internet to try and move the train, resulting in countless videos that have cropped up from those seeking to test its mettle (and farm a bit of engagement on social media).
Naturally, GTA 6 presented an updated take on the opportunity when players discovered its train. Unfortunately, Rockstar's commitment to realism means moving the new locomotive isn't just possible; it's actually kind of easy. Crash into it with a dump truck? Works like a charm. Park an excavator in its path? Stops it in its tracks. Raise a bridge? Completely detailed. Rockstar's new, smarter NPCs even have the brains to pull the brakes when they see a person simply standing in their way.
This is where we get into the argument that has plagued Rockstar both inside and outside of the studio for years: When is a game too realistic? Judging by GTA 6's record-breaking earnings and all-time great reviews, it seems the developers' new playground struck a nice balance between being grounded and goofy. Of course, that hasn't stopped a small section of players from being upset that Leonida plays by many of the same rules that we do in the real world.
After GTA 5's train spent more than a decade as the running champ of viral videos to come out of Los Santos, players aren't ready to let GTA 5's train go. In fact, some have began to almost deify the 2013 locomotive, creating fan edits showing the last train as the superior vehicle in the locomotive power-scaling battle.
"Yeah, this and the 'No first-person mode' are the biggest downsides for me," one X/Twitter user said.

@leviackermanft Meanwhile, GTA V: https://t.co/C2X01m6McJ

item.title: You can use GTA 6's Waink app to scan specific magazines to unlock new hairstyles for Jason, as well as hair and makeup looks for Lucia.
item.description:
We all know that finding magazines around Leonida is one of GTA's collectible quests, and we all know that the Waink app can be used to scan cars for information or street art. It turns out that it can also be used to scan specific magazines to unlock new hairstyles for Jason, as well as hair and makeup looks for Lucia — but these magazines are significantly harder to find.
I found one sitting by a chair in a random, but otherwise pretty boring part of Key Lento. It's not a magazine you can pick up and read like the collectible ones, but a scan with the Waink app unlocked a new Pop Star makeup style. It's apparently one of 15 "Lucia Magazine Styles" to unlock, and I imagine it's a similar number of facial hair and hair unlocks for Jason.
Rockstar has confirmed that additional hairstyles are available in GTA 6, including those offered through the Vintage Vice City Pack, but it hasn’t published official instructions detailing how Waink’s hairstyle unlocks work. It's just another one of those fun little secrets that players have been left to find for themselves. So far I've only found one, but I'm now on a very serious hunt for the rest. The good news is that you do get a Waink prompt when you're close to one, so if you've been in any stores or locations wondering what the hell was setting it off, this might have been the answer.
This has now unlocked a whole new collectibles obsession for me, as if the books, magazines, collectible cars, birds, street art, and everything else you can find in our official guide weren't enough. This game will never let me know peace again.

item.title: Earlier today, Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, after two weeks of scandals involving multiple affairs and a suspected spy. But while he's back in the pilot's seat, Huang's problems aren't over, and he's been summoned to testify in front of the US Senate.
item.description:
Earlier today, Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, after two weeks of scandals involving multiple affairs and a suspected spy. Although he's back in the pilot's seat, Huang's problems aren't over, as he's been summoned to testify in front of the U.S. Senate.
Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify in front of the Senate's Banking Committee on December 3, according to Bloomberg. The hearing was announced by the committee's chairman, Tim Scott, and will focus on oversight of U.S. export controls. That comes just a week after Nvidia announced that it would be establishing a National Security and Export Control Committee last week.
Huang's appearance in front of the Banking Committee is only the latest hearing that's been announced. Huang is also scheduled to appear in front of three House committees in two closed-doors meetings on December 1 and December 2. While those congressional hearings will be closed to the public, they will be transcribed, and will likely also be covering Nvidia's adherance to U.S. export controls.
Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 – Photos
But while Huang will now have to testify in front of both houses of Congress, his reinstatement came after President Donald Trump intervened on his behalf. In Nvidia's own statement about the CEO's return, it said, "In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk." It turns out that input came from President Trump, who called the board and gave "reassurances" that Huang's return wouldn't pose a national security risk.
While the President acted to have Huang reinstated, plenty of representatives from both parties have demanded answers on social media. Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren posted, saying, "This reckless decision to bring back Jensen Huang does not change the fact that Huang and NVIDIA still owe Congress answers. The Trump Administration needs to explain what 'input' was given and by which senior officials to support Huang’s reinstatement."
At the same time, Republican Senator John Curtis posted, "Nvidia’s board says it relied on input from senior U.S. officials to conclude that bringing Jensen Huang back posed no national security risk. I have some questions. Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board? And on what basis did the board conclude there was no risk?"
While this scandal built up steam in the background for months, it really exploded two weeks ago, when Huang admitted to an affair that kicked off an internal investigation into his conduct. He resigned just a few days later, and even though the board came out and said Huang wouldn't be reinstated, he reclaimed his office earlier today.
Photo by Nadja Wohlleben/Getty Images.

item.title: The estate of late American R&B artist D’Angelo has spoken out after the launch of GTA 6, which featured a song that he created for the game back in 2024.
item.description:
The estate of late American R&B artist D’Angelo has spoken out after the launch of GTA 6, which featured a song that he created for the game back in 2024.
GTA 6 features a slew of songs, both licensed and original, from a wide variety of high-profile music artists. Names like Cardi B, Tame Impala, Burna Boy, and many more contributed to the game’s soundtrack. D’Angelo was one of those artists who created a track for the game two years ahead of its highly anticipated November 2026 launch.
The song, titled ‘Kamikaze,’ is a funky tune that players quickly discovered during their playthroughs. Snippets of the track were uploaded to social media mere days after GTA 6’s release, and now, D’Angelo’s estate has officially confirmed the track’s existence in the game.
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
The track and its title were shared on November 23, 2026, in a series of Instagram posts on D’Angelo’s official profile. One of these included a statement penned by his brother, Luther Archer, who described how
“Michael approved this track in its current form in November of 2024 to be released as part of Grand Theft Auto VI. He was a tremendous admirer of Rockstar Games and a past collaborator of theirs, and he was enthusiastic (to say the least) to have this record included in the game and released to a wide audience as a single,” Archer wrote.
“Kamikazi was produced by D'Angelo himself, with Slingbaum and engineer/trusted ally Ben Kane. It features performances from D'Angelo and Slingbaum alongside Yussef Dayes (drums on the left) and the late legendary James Gadson (drums on the right). The cover artwork was done by Andre Trenier, the genius brother of Michael's mentor and longtime manager Dominque Trenier.”
D’Angelo has a storied history with Rockstar; he created a song for the Red Dead Redemption 2 soundtrack titled ‘May I? Stand Unshaken,’ a collaboration that came about after he asked to playtest the game at Rockstar’s New York Offices before its release.
“D’Angelo’s actually a massive, massive, massive fan of the game — more than I ever knew,” Rockstar Games’ Director of Music and Audio, Ivan Pavlovich, told Rolling Stone in a 2018 interview.
“He would come in here [Rockstar’s New York city office] and just play the game. We weren’t even talking about doing music. When D’Angelo comes through, he shows up at midnight, and he’s playing the game until four in the morning. Each time he was just like, ‘It’s incredible.’ It just blows his mind. He’s such a fan. I have never seen someone that excited.”
D’Angelo died of pancreatic cancer at the age of 51 in October 2025. Since then, his brother, Luther Archer, has taken over the task of releasing his posthumous works — one of which is featured in the biggest media release of all time from a company that was near and dear to D’Angelo’s heart.

item.title: One of GTA 6's biggest controversies was Rockstar's decision to keep the game's framerate locked at 30 fps, rather than allowing for an unlocked mode. Over the weekend, players managed to find a glitch on Xbox Series X that lets you unlock the frame rate, albeit to mixed results.
item.description:
One of GTA 6's biggest controversies was Rockstar's decision to keep the game's framerate locked at 30fps, rather than allowing for an unlocked mode. Over the weekend, players managed to find a glitch on Xbox Series X that lets you unlock the frame rate, albeit to mixed results.
The glitch is performed by booting up the game when the Xbox console is set to 60fps, then going into the console settings, switching the system to 120fps, launching another game, and then using Quick Resume to start GTA 6 back up. That process essentially tricks the system into unlocking the frame rate, and some people have been able to push it a bit higher than the game's default 30fps lock.
The folks over at Digital Foundry were able to put the '60fps glitch' to the test, though, and found that while you could push upwards of 60fps, it was limited to situations where, "If you look straight up in the ocean, frame-rates can just about graze 60fps."
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
Instead, Digital Foundry's results reaffirm Rockstar's decision to ship the game with a 30fps lock. While the game managed an average of 36fps in the first hour of the game, GTA 6 only gets more demanding as it progresses into Vice City, where NPCs and explosions are both more prevalent. And, in those situations, the game still has sharp drops to lower frame rates.
The whole reason a 30fps cap makes sense for GTA 6 is consistency. While this glitch shows that the game sometimes has the headroom to peek above 30fps, and even into the 40s, getting rid of the cap would just mean the difference between the peaks and valleys of the frame rate would be even higher, and thus more noticeable. It's no secret that the game does drop below 30 fps during heavy action or when you're speeding through the world, but any dip from 40fps to 24fps would be a lot more jarring than a dip from 30fps to 24fps.
This glitch has given some fans renewed hope that an unlocked version of the game would come out at some point, but Rockstar has been pretty clear about this generation's technical limitations. Right as GTA 6 was coming out, Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers flat-out said that the PS5 Pro processor "is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates." That's something I've noticed myself as I've started to cause more problems in Vice City.
Still, it would be nice to play GTA 6 at a higher frame rate, even if I have to wait for the PC version to do so. Luckily, it does seem like a PC port will be coming faster than previous entries, due to Rockstar's worry about an unofficial and AI-assisted port of the game. It's even starting to look like its fears on that front were justified.

item.title: A YouTuber has solved the wildest GTA 6 Easter egg puzzle yet in just three days. Here's how he did it, and what he found at the end.
item.description:
A YouTuber has uncovered the wildest GTA 6 Easter egg yet. Following a series of arcane clues and pulling a set of switches in the correct order sees players transported back to the 1980s.
Warning! Spoilers for GTA 6 follow.
The Easter egg begins in the R&D tower in Key Lento, GTA 6’s starting area, but spans almost the entire map. Players have to pull a series of switches and press certain buttons to trigger a portal into the past, complete with new voice acting from Danny Dyer as Kent Paul.
After scaling the tower, the YouTuber (Memeio) noticed that a sound effect from GTA Vice City plays when he messed with the lever and button. A poster for LPL (Leonida Power and Light) in the room then guided him around Leonida to the LPL power substations dotted around the map.
GTA 6 Bikini Girl Screenshots
Each substation contained letters written on its walls. Memeio was so committed to figuring out the mystery that he actually followed the power cables across the map to track them all down.
After putting all the letters together from all 12 substations, Memeio realized they spelled out an interesting phrase: “Life is passing me by.” That phrase was a cheat code in Vice City that sped up the in-game clock.
On PlayStation, the code for that cheat was: Circle, L1, Square, L1, Square, L1, Triangle, Circle, Triangle.
Memeio realized that he had to enter that code using all the buttons and switches at the various substations, applying a button to different lever flips and button presses. After pressing the buttons in order, without fast travelling, Memeio got an in-game text to head to Reactor 2 between 7pm and 6am. When he did, a portal opened.
Stepping through the portal transported him to Vice City’s Malibu Club, complete with polygonal graphics. Upstairs, he even saw Kent Paul, voiced by British actor Danny Dyer, reprising his role. Danny Dyer is included in the credits for GTA 6 under the “local population" category.
For all that effort, you get access to Tommy Vercetti’s iconic floral shirt and his classic Malibu bike, complete with star decals.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 has everything you could possibly want from a video game: crime, chaos, expensive cars, and, apparently, the ability to end your real-life relationship.
item.description:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has everything you could possibly want from a video game: crime, chaos, expensive cars, and, apparently, the ability to end your real-life relationship.
Social media is filling up with people claiming GTA 6 has caused them to break up with their significant others. Some are apparently fed up with their partners spending more time in Vice City than with them, while others seem to have discovered that a fictional romance between two career criminals is somehow setting unrealistic expectations for their own love lives. And while I'm sure there are genuine arguments happening in households across the world right now, I'm going to need a little more convincing that people are actually ending their relationships over Rockstar's latest game.
My homie going thru it with his girl over GTA 6 she threatening to break up with bro🤦🏻‍♂️🤣
my roommate and her bf are genuinely about to break up over gta 6 LMFAOOOO
It's true that GTA 6 is the biggest entertainment launch of all time. It's the sort of game that people have been planning their lives around for years, booking time off work, clearing their schedules, and presumably warning loved ones that they might not be emotionally available for the foreseeable future. That's hardly conducive to a healthy relationship, particularly if one half of the couple has absolutely no interest in video games. But there's a difference between being annoyed that your boyfriend has spent 14 consecutive hours driving around Leonida and packing your bags because he won't stop playing.
GTA 6 is actually about to end my relationship https://t.co/UsOJlQQvIt
There's also the Jason and Lucia factor. GTA 6's central couple have become something of a social media phenomenon, particularly thanks to the optional romantic gestures that allow Jason to be an attentive boyfriend. He can buy flowers, open car doors, and generally behave like someone who understands that being in a relationship involves occasionally doing something nice for the other person.
On the other side, some people are claiming that they truly consider investing time in the couple's relationship as cheating, a response that seems to come purely from people seeing that Lucia is attractive, or thanks to misconceptions about sex workers, strip clubs, or the in-game intimacy options. In fact, 19% of polled respondents said they would "not be okay" with their partner spending time on fictional relationships in a video game, as per a YouGov poll published October 2026.
Of course, social media has never been particularly concerned with letting the truth get in the way of a good post. Announcing that you've dumped your boyfriend because he loves GTA 6 more than you do is practically engineered to generate engagement. It gets the gamers angry, the relationship commentators become involved, and everyone else arguing in the replies. One that's gone particulary viral is a woman in her bathroom claiming that she's getting divorced specifically because her husband won't stop playing. It's worth noting that her other posts on the topic say 'satire 'in the discussions, and this one says, "For entertainment purposes only!!!"
Another Instagram post about a supposed break up has the same influencer telling a story about being accused of cheating because she was playing GTA 6 online with someone else's boyfriend. GTA 6 does not currently have an online or co-op mode, so it's worth taking these types of posts with a healthy grain of salt.
That's not to say gaming can't cause genuine friction between couples; if your partner is consistently ignoring you, neglecting responsibilities, or treating your relationship like an irritating side quest, that's a problem. But it's probably an issue that existed well before GTA 6 arrived. Are people genuinely breaking up over GTA 6? Possibly. Are some people exaggerating for attention? Almost certainly. Until there's more than a handful of viral posts to go on, I'm inclined to remain skeptical. Besides, if your relationship can be destroyed by a video game, I suspect Rockstar wasn't the real villain here.

item.title: Canadian streaming service Crave has greenlit the mystery thriller series Yaga for a second season, with Carrie-Anne Moss confirmed to return.
item.description:
Canadian streaming service Crave has greenlit the mystery thriller series Yaga for a second season with Carrie-Anne Moss confirmed to return. The decision comes prior to Season 1's two-episode finale on November 27.
Yaga debuted on October 23 and quickly became #1 on Crave. It also took the top spot for its biggest "exclusive series launch ever" on AMC+ in the U.S., along with holding the #1 position in multiple other countries around the world.
“The incredible response to Yaga has blown us away,” Justin Stockman, vice president of global content for Bell Media said in a press release. “Congratulations to Kat Sandler and our production partners at Blink49 Studios and Front Street Pictures. Together, we’ve created a bold and daring Canadian series that we believe strongly in, and we can’t wait to see where Season 2 takes us.”
Yaga: Season 1 Photo Gallery
Pancho Mansfield, president of global scripted at Blink49 Studios, added, “Kat Sandler has brought such a bold and distinctive vision to Yaga, and we’re incredibly proud to have supported her in bringing it to the screen. To see her first television series as creator and showrunner resonate with audiences in Canada and around the world has been enormously rewarding. We’re thrilled to continue our partnership with Bell Media to bring the next chapter of Yaga to life.”
For those unfamiliar, Yaga is a modern retelling of the European folklore around Baba Yaga – a witch who takes on the role of both villain and mentor, harnessing both good and evil depending on the story. The new series is from Kat Sandler, who created a stage play of the same name and serves as writer, showrunner, and executive producer.

item.title: Hiroyuki Sanada has reportedly entered final negotiations to play Hiruzen Sarutobi in Destin Daniel Cretton's live-action Naruto movie.
item.description:
Hiroyuki Sanada has reportedly entered final negotiations to play Hiruzen Sarutobi in Destin Daniel Cretton's live-action Naruto movie.
The Mortal Kombat and Shogun actor's potential role in the anime-to-film adaptation was first reported by Deadline. Should talks with Cretton and Lionsgate check those last few boxes, he will appear as the Hidden Leaf Village's Hokage leader.
How Sanada may help the iconic Hokage lead to the big screen remains to be seen. Meanwhile, the site's report stated that Charles Melton (Warfare, Beef Season 2), who was said to be in final negotiations to play Kakashi back in August, is still in talks to join Naruto.
The Spider-Man: Brand New Day director's shot at bringing one of the most beloved manga and anime properties of all time into the live-action realm is expected to begin filming sometime in spring 2027. With production right around the corner, though, Sony and Lionsgate have shared little about which actors have been picked to play some of the franchise's most important roles.
The only names we've heard so far are Melton and Sanada, and even their parts in the story haven't been outright confirmed just yet. Depending on what story Cretton and company hope to tell, there is still plenty of room for additional casting updates. Names like Sasuke, Sakura, and, of course, Naruto still have no names publicly attached, though that doesn't necessarily mean that stars haven't been picked behind the scenes.
Lionsgate confirmed it had initiated a global casting search for actors to play the leads in the live-action Naruto picture. Specifically, it said it was on the lookout for stars for Team 7, suggesting the actors picked to appear as Naruto, Sasuke, and Sakura could be unknown names in the movie space.
Naruto x Silverlake Ramen Collab
"[Naruto creator Masashi Kishimoto-sensei's] stories have inspired generations of fans around the world, and it’s an honor to bring his world and characters to the big screen in live action for the very first time," Cretton said at the time of the global casting search reveal. "I'm thrilled to kick off this worldwide casting search for our Team 7 and to bring the incredible universe of Naruto to life!"
The live-action Naruto movie currently has no release date. For more, you can check out Kishimoto's new manga tease. You can also catch up on how to watch all of Naruto in order.
Photo by Amy Sussman/Getty Images.

item.title: Nice-guy Fortnite streamer Nick Eh 30 has gone viral after trying GTA 6 — and immediately pushing the violence in Rockstar's game to its limit.
item.description:
Nice-guy Fortnite streamer Nick Eh 30 has gone viral after trying GTA 6 — and immediately pushing the violence in Rockstar's game to its limit.
For almost a decade, cheery Canadian streamer Nicholas "Nick Eh 30" Amyoony has amassed a community of millions around his family-friendly Fortnite streams. His personal brand is based on pushing positivity, he's known for never swearing on camera, and he's become one of the few Twitch stars partnered with Epic Games to get a skin of himself made available in-game.
So it has, understandably, come as something of a surprise to see wholesome Nick Eh 30 embracing the most dastardly deeds GTA 6 has on offer: kicking pet dogs to death in the street, shooting animals in the zoo, and walking down the length of a train executing every passenger at point blank range.
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
As someone who has followed Nick Eh 30 for a while, seeing him wandering around GTA 6's world eliminating swathes of its animal population while chuckling to himself is indeed odd to see. Social media is awash with similar reactions, with posts from his followers stating things like: "IN WHAT UNIVERSE DO YOU NEED TO BE DOING THIS" and "Years of building ramps in Fortnite could not prepare chat for this."
But this is all clearly intentional, down to his streams being labelled as humorously promising "family friendly GTA" gameplay (I'm not sure there's any such thing). And the fact this has led people to actually discuss his streams and share clips further has only proven why he's likely doing this.
NickEh30 takes a taser to the Zoo in GTA VI https://t.co/4SAVgUCjYm
All of that said, it's still a surprise to see Nick squarely aiming for the game's brutal "Irredeemable" criminal profile rating — a label that Rockstar has actually made quite difficult to achieve unless you really, really want to play the game as bloodily as possible.
It's this, seemingly, which has led to clips of Nick playing fetch with dogs using lumps of C4, and throwing random NPCs from buildings.

item.title: Marvel Studios has released a new Avengers: Doomsday poster that gives us our closest look at Doctor Doom's mask yet.
item.description:
Marvel Studios has released a new Avengers: Doomsday poster that gives us our closest look at Doctor Doom's mask yet.
Robert Downey Jr.'s Victor von Doom debut is almost here. This new poster arrives hot on the heels of the movie's newest trailer, and while it focused on Steve Roger's (Chris Evans) role in the chaos, the poster gives one of the most iconic masks in comic book history the attention it deserves.
Considering all of the hubbub about Doctor Doom's different masks and costumes, it's nice to get a close-up of one of his most menacing looks and Downey Jr.'s dark green eye. You can see the full poster below.
Impressive details and rusty edges aside, many have also pointed out that there's more to this poster than meets the eye. No, there are no fun theories circulating about this one (yet), but it does continue to play into Downey Jr.'s ties to both Doctor Doom and his original Marvel Cinematic Universe hero, Iron Man.
One of the earliest MCU posters offered the same look at Iron Man's original Mark 3 design. Where Tony's poster gave audiences a new hero to take seriously, Doctor Doom's poster is more of a reminder of how far Marvel's heroes have come — and how far they still have to fall.
The reference is impossible to deny as fans continue to speculate how both of Downey Jr.'s characters may be connected. So far, Marvel has done its best to convince viewers that Doctor Doom is not a Tony Stark variant, but with posters like this only making the line between them darker, it's clear the MCU has more than a few fun surprises in store for next month.
@JetSetHan @MarvelStudios https://t.co/vGpTdzASk2
Avengers: Doomsday premieres December 18, 2026. Despite keeping the fate of the Avengers, New Avengers, X-Men, and Fantastic Four a mystery, Marvel has drip-fed fans new information in the lead-up to launch. Last week, we got a look at a series of new, smaller posters, with an even earlier poster teasing Doctor Doom's Latverian witches. Just yesterday, Kate Bishop actress Hailee Steinfeld joined the cast.
For more, you can check out how Hot Toys revealed an alternate look at the MCU's new big bad. You can also see Downey Jr. tease more from the film with a new behind-the-scenes video.

item.title: Steven Spielberg is going big with his next film, which is a Western written by Paul Thomas Anderson and starring Cillian Murphy.
item.description:
Steven Spielberg is going big with his next film, which is a Western written by Paul Thomas Anderson and starring Cillian Murphy.
Deadline confirmed that Spielberg is already developing his next film following the release of Disclosure Day this summer, and it'll be an adaptation of the 2024 novel The Heart in Winter. The book is set in 1891 amid a harsh winter in a Montana mining town. It follows a degenerate poet and ballad-maker who crosses paths with the new bride of the town's mine captain, sparking an intense love affair before they run west together with pursuers hot on their tail. Spielberg described the project to Deadline as a story about "people who refused to settle for a life that is less than they deserve but maybe more than they can handle."
Cillian Murphy and Jessie Buckley will play the leading characters in the film, which is apparently still untitled despite being sourced from an existing piece of work. He has also teamed with Oscar-winner Paul Thomas Anderson, who is penning the script. This marks the first time Anderson has fully written a script that he himself hasn't directed, but he has done uncredited punch-ups and rewrites on other movies like Killers of the Flower Moon.
The 10 Best Steven Spielberg Movies of All Time
“It’s really the excitement for me to get to work together with my dear friend and colleague Paul Thomas Anderson on a genre, but more particularly, the genre notwithstanding, a story that quite quickly became close to both our hearts and we felt that we could do as a team," said Spielberg about the partnership.
The two began flirting with the idea of working together back in January while Anderson was on the awards trail for One Battle After Another, which cleaned up at the various ceremonies and led to him receiving an Oscar for Best Adapted Screenplay. Naturally, that kind of prestige makes him a smart pick to adapt a layered novel such as this one. The two binged old Westerns on 35mm film as part of their creative process.
Spielberg's untitled Western is currently targeting a 2028 release, with filming set to begin next winter. The 79-year-old director was also quick to note that this is not his final project and denied that this was some kind of metaphor about his career, where he gets to literally ride off into the sunset at the end.
“If I wanted to ride off into the sunset, I would have done Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade next, and I could have had those characters literally riding off into the sunset as the credits roll,” Spielberg said.
Photo by Presley Ann/Getty Images for Lucas Museum of Narrative Art

item.title: The internet is reacting to Jensen Huang's shock return as Nvidia CEO.
item.description:
Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO following two weeks of scandals involving alleged affairs, with one involving a suspected spy.
Just last week, Nvidia CFO Collette Kress, who served as interim CEO during Huang's absence, had ruled out that he would return, and the company also took the opportunity to implement a new oversight committee to prevent more security scandals in the future.
While Nvidia was picking up the pieces, Huang went on his own journey to return to Nvidia, putting out a statement suggesting he would be willing to return as CEO if the board thought it would be best for the company. And, well, it seems like that's exactly what happened. In a press release issued earlier this morning, Nvidia Board Chair Harvey C. Jones said: "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers."
Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 – Photos
It does seem like the U.S. Government played a big role in Huang's return. Nvidia's own statement says, "In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk." President Donald Trump has also been posting through it, most recently saying that, "I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A."
But in the hours since Huang's return, it's become clear just how much Trump tipped the scales in his favor. Trump spoke with Nvidia's board and brokered a deal to ensure his return, according to an interview with CNBC. Beyond saying that he "convinced them" and "made the deal," Trump gave Nvidia assurances over the national security implications. According to Trump: "And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot."
Trump then called Huang personally, telling CNBC: "He knows what to do and what not to do. But I just said work hard because if you work hard, there’s nobody that can capture what you’ve done. Nobody, nobody close."
According to CBS senior White House correspondent Weijia Jiang, "Trump says if Huang had not been reinstated at Nvidia, Xi might have called and asked him to lead a Chinese company. If Huang was 'mad' enough at the U.S. Trump said he may have done it… adding he has some of their 'blood in him.'"
Trump wasn't acting alone. According to Semafor White House correspondent Shelby Talcott, Vice President JD Vance played a big role in Huang's return too. Talcott tweeted: "VP JD Vance was deeply involved in the process to bring Jensen Huang back to Nvidia. He and POTUS were 'personally engaged' over the weekend to resolve the situation, a source familiar tells me — Vance used his relationships in Silicon Valley + business community to help move the Nvidia board along."
Nvidia bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO was always going to be a controversial move, but the Trump administration's role in the shocking development has caused backlash online.
Over on the Nvidia subreddit, most of the comments are calling out alleged corruption, with the top comment quoting Nvidia's input from the government, with the first reply saying, "lmaooo It's f**king hilarious to watch how corrupt that country is now." Another comment in the same thread simply says: "The USA is truly the most corrupt country among democracies."
In our own comments, user Killarogue added: "Society is broken. This dude should be investigated, and if the reports are true, sent to prison for illegally selling chips to customers in China. Specifically the H200 chips to blacklisted customers within China." While another user, ZeroZep, said: "Pretty disgusting but I guess that’s par for course in the society we live in today. Now let’s see the spy and shady business practice allegations magically go away too."
Meanwhile, on social media, the White House tweeted out Trump's thoughts on Huang's return: "The Nvidia Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO… Congratulations to Jensen, the Nvidia Board, to the People of the United States — and, indeed, the World!" There was also a critical mass of AI-generated gifs of Huang returning to the office.
At the same time, Illinois Governor JB Pritzker tweeted: "This is the greed and lack of accountability that the country just rejected. There are serious national security concerns being raised about Jensen Huang that should not be papered over by this administration or the Nvidia board."
Utah Senator John Curtis also had questions, posting on Twitter: "Nvidia’s board says it relied on input from senior U.S. officials to conclude that bringing Jensen Huang back posed no national security risk. I have some questions. Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board? And on what basis did the board conclude there was no risk?"
MSNBC's Sam Stein added: "I think it's worth being candid about what happened here. The U.S. government pressured the board of a private company to reinstate a CEO who had compromised U.S. national security and broken serious internal HR policies because they liked what he did to the share price."
But amid corruption concerns, there were plenty of people joking about the timing of Huang's return. Rapper Lotus Juice tweeted: "Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO? It’s almost like he took time off just for GTA6 lol"
Gamer's Nexus also joked about Huang's return, referencing Morrowind's classic "with this character's death, the thred of prophecy is severed," along with a caption that simply says: "Quick load."
Only time will tell if this saga is actually over, and what the long-term ramifications are going to be. During the course of Huang's absense, new allegations arose about his management style, and at one point Elon Musk even floated the idea of hiring him.
Photo by Sean Gallup/Getty Images.

item.title: Brad Pitt has given a promising update on the status of World War Z 2, a film that has been in development hell for over a decade.
item.description:
Brad Pitt has given a promising update on the status of World War Z 2, a film that has been in development hell for over a decade.
In 2013, Paramount released World War Z starring Brad Pitt, which became the highest-grossing zombie flick of all time. The movie itself wasn't anything to write home about, outside of a couple of cool action scenes, but it was a solid crowd-pleaser. And yet, Hollywood has been trying to crack the code on a follow-up for years. For a while, David Fincher was set to direct a sequel with Pitt returning, but that eventually fell apart. After that, it seemed like the project was dead.
However, as part of Skydance's new initiative to revitalize certain IP, leadership wants to prioritize a new World War Z film. When speaking with Collider, Pitt gave a small yet promising update on the film, which he believes could start shooting as soon as next year if they manage to lock down a script. He noted that they're "talking zombie logic" and polishing the script currently, trying to figure out a fresh angle on the genre.
"The thing is, it's well-worn territory," said Pitt in reference to zombie genre being somewhat saturated. "How do we keep it fresh? How do we take it somewhere it hasn't gone before? We've got some good ideas that I'm pretty excited about. We're fleshing them out now."
Should the film come to fruition, it will be directed by Edward Berger, who has directed acclaimed films such as Conclave and 2022's All Quiet on the Western Front. Pitt will also begin working on Ocean's 14, the fourth film in the heist film franchise, sometime next year, as well.
Despite being 62 years old, Pitt clearly isn't backing down from his leading man role, particularly when it comes to intense and demanding action films like World War Z 2. As of right now, we'll just have to wait and see what happens. Does anyone really want a sequel to this movie 13 years later? It doesn't really seem like there's a flurry of demand for it, but at least the people behind the film seem passionate about it.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Deborah Ann Woll will reprise her role as Faye in Prime Video's live-action God of War show.
item.description:
Deborah Ann Woll will reprise her role as Faye in Prime Video's live-action God of War show.
It's the casting update everyone has been waiting for, even if some were worried it may never happen. Woll, who played the god-like character in God of War Ragnarok and will lead her own installment with God of War Laufey in 2027, will officially play the live-action version of Faye for the show.
"The mysterious late wife of Kratos and mother of Atreus, Faye's abrupt passing sets in motion the events of God of War," an official description shared by Amazon said. "Along their journey, Kratos and Atreus discover secrets about Faye that make them wonder how well they truly knew her at all."
Despite only physically appearing in one game thus far, Faye is a character who already has deep ties to Kratos and the rest of the series. In the franchise's 2018 installment, Faye serves as Kratos and Atreus' faceless guide as the father and son work to spread her ashes in Jötunheim.
Although their mission to let go of a powerful warrior, mother, and wife came to an end in the 2018 game, she continued to play an important role as Kratos faced the wrath of Norse gods like Thor and Odin in God of War Ragnarok in 2022. It was here that Woll first played the character, though only for a small portion of an otherwise meaty adventure.
Prime Video's God of War show picking Woll to return in live-action makes sense for more reasons than one. Besides also being set to spearhead God of War Laufey when it releases in May 2027, Woll is a proven talent with a live-action resume that plenty of movie and TV fans are already more than familiar with. In addition to notable roles in projects like True Blood, Escape Room, and The Cycle, she's also prominently played the role of Karen Page in Marvel projects like Daredevil and its Born Again follow-up show, as well as The Punisher.
God Of War Laufey Reveal
"God of War follows father and son Kratos and Atreus as they embark on a journey to spread the ashes of their wife and mother, Faye," a series logline says. "Through their adventures, Kratos tries to teach his son to be a better god, while Atreus tries to teach his father how to be a better human."
The God of War series has no firm release date yet, and for good reason. After first casting Ryan Hurst as Kratos earlier this year, an unfortunate on-set injury led the project to recast the lead role. Guardians of the Galaxy and Knives Out alum Dave Bautista will now play the Leviathan Axe-wielding protagonist, with Callum Vinson still set as Atreus.
The show's cast also includes Mandy Patinkin as Odin, Ed Skrein as Baldur, Teresa Palmer as Sif, and more. Alastair Duncan will also reprise his role as Mimir. Since we already know Thor and Odin will show up, we can guess Prime Video's God of War story will be somewhat different from the games it draws from.
Photo by Corey Nickols/Getty Images for IMDb.

item.title: Cyberleek has reportedly made good on their promise and released the executable file for the leaked Xbox build of GTA 6, sparking concern that an unofficial PC port could be around the corner.
item.description:
Cyberleek has reportedly made good on their promise and released the executable file for the leaked Xbox build of GTA 6, sparking concern that an unofficial PC port could be around the corner.
The infamous hacker had vowed to release the .exe for the incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build whether the Cyberleek memecoin hit its market cap target or not, and now it is out in the wild, some within the homebrew scene are preparing to take a close look at it.
Cyberleek released the exe with a fresh statement insisting their actions on GTA 6 so far were about “fighting anti-consumerism in the games industry.” Cyberleek also taunts Rockstar parent company Take-Two’s so-far unsuccessful effort to prevent further leaks or, it seems, track down those responsible, saying: “Months of takedowns, subpoenas and wallet tracing later, the hunt is still on and the uploads keep arriving.”
GTA 6 Bikini Girl Screenshots
They also pushed back on claims the GTA 6 leaks are about little more than pushing a crypto scheme, insisting that crypto was used to generate funds for a secret project outside of the game. “There is no other way to move funds without names,” Cyberleek said, “and this work requires no names.”
Some are now predicting that AI-assisted recompilation of the leaked Xbox build could result in GTA 6 on PC in just days, with performance improvements over the console version in weeks.
This is of course a nightmare scenario for Take-Two and Sony and Microsoft, which are benefiting greatly from GTA 6 releasing on console only. The console version of GTA 6 targets 30fps across all platforms, although struggles at times to hit that on base PS5, and Xbox Series X and S. As a result, there is huge interest in a potential PC version offering 60fps gameplay.
The release of the Xbox build from this month runs counter to the thought that Cyberleek only had access to an early development build of GTA 6, a feeling that was reinforced not only by the videos that were released in the summer, but by the differences that have emerged following the game’s official launch.
Fans are calling on people not to spend money on Cyberleek, pointing out the leaker cashed out back in August and did again in October. Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker cashing out having earnt around $270,000.
IGN had reported on fan skepticism around the alleged leaked gameplay that reportedly showed both Jason and Lucia fully naked. A previous leaked gameplay video allegedly showed a tank spawning into the world, which suggested access to a dev menu of some kind. The leaked videos allegedly showing both Jason and Lucia fully naked also show NPCs failing to react to that in any way, which suggested this effect was achieved with either a dev menu or cheats.
In the wake of Cyberleek’s initial leaks, Take-Two issued subpoenas to the likes of Discord as part of its search for the person or group of people responsible. It remains unclear how the gameplay footage, any potential build of the game it was taken from, or this latest Xbox build, escaped the confines of Rockstar's infamous tight security.
In August, Rockstar addressed the GTA 6 leaks, describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. At the time, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19.

item.title: The hacker behind the massive GTA 6 leak in September 2022 has been released on license with a strong warning from the judge.
item.description:
The hacker behind the massive GTA 6 leak in September 2022 has been released on license with a strong warning from the judge. Having already served the majority of his seven year sentence, Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford in the United Kingdom, was allowed to go free, conditionally.
According to the BBC, the judge warned Kurtaj: "Don't let this happen again."
Kurtaj attempted to extort GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games in 2022. After socially engineering his way into the company Slack, the now 21-year-old threatened to release clips of the unfinished game unless Rockstar paid a ransom. He pleaded guilty to the hacking offenses, which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old, earlier this week.
⚖️ Arion Kurtaj, 21, has been convicted today for targeting major international companies, hacking into their private systems, stealing information and data, and causing millions of dollars in losses. 📰 https://t.co/UvJTCFWnct https://t.co/3CoLIw7dDs
Originally, Kurtaj was sentenced to an indefinite stay in a prison hospital due to his autism diagnosis. After reconsideration, he was deemed fit to stand trial and spent the remainder of his time in a traditional prison, starting in January.
With his release, Kurtaj has been given a Serious Crime Prevention Order, which restricts his interactions online, barring him from using social apps like Telegram and Discord, in an attempt to prevent him working with hacker groups. The order will last for five years.
The hack happened while Kurtaj was already under police protection in a Travelodge with his computer confiscated. During his stay, he used an Amazon Fire Stick and the hotel television to hack Rockstar, Revolut, and Uber.
GTA 6 Bikini Girl Screenshots
The GTA 6 hack saw him steal 90 clips of an unfinished build well before Rockstar was ready to show gameplay from its anticipated open-world sequel, which launched last week. It resulted in the first major GTA 6 leak, as early gameplay footage was shared online. Here, we saw dual protagonists Jason and Lucia for the first time. These clips were shared under the online name TeaPotUberHacker. It would be over a year before Rockstar finally showed the protagonists itself, and even longer until we got an official gameplay reveal, which was only shared in August of this year.
"If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code," he said in the company Slack. When the company didn’t respond, he released the files, costing the company $5 million in damages.

item.title: Daredevil star Charlie Cox says he was denied a James Bond audition after being told he was already "too old" to play 007.
item.description:
Daredevil star Charlie Cox says he was denied a James Bond audition after being told he was already "too old" to play 007, prior to the casting of Twilight and Batman star Robert Pattinson.
Despite spending the past decade throwing himself into brutal hallway brawls, Cox said he couldn't even audition to be the new James Bond because of his age. Speaking today on Virgin Radio, the 43-year-old Marvel star said he'd asked his agent about becoming the new 00 agent, only to be quickly shut down.
"I asked to audition for that, do you know what they told me? Too old," Cox laughed, admitting that he didn't even make it into an audition room. "Rob's the same age as me!" he continued, before being told that, actually, the Batman actor is three years younger.
"What an amazing career that guy's carved out," Cox said, praising Pattinson for getting the part. "Some of the stuff he's done, the directors he's worked with... just amazing."
The Next James Bonds Who Never Played 007
While Cox wouldn't have been the oldest actor cast as James Bond, he would have certainly been on the older end. Sean Connery was 32 years old when he gained 007 status, George Lazenby was 30 years old, Roger Moore was 45 years old, Timothy Dalton was 41 years old, Pierce Brosnan was 42 years old, and Daniel Craig was 38 years old.
Still, for fans who have watched Cox effortlessly pull off both sharp-suited charm as Matt Murdock and relentless physical stunts as his superhero alter ego, ruling the actor out immediately is a shame — particularly now his crime-fighting days may be nearing an end with Disney's culling of Daredevil: Born Again following its forthcoming third season.
Pattinson's casting as Bond ended years of speculation over who would take on the role, and months of unusually detailed reporting on the actors who came close behind Pattinson in the running. Callum Turner (One Night Only) and Jacob Elordi (Euphoria) were two faces talked about earlier on, with Slow Horses star Jack Lowden then entering the conversation shortly after. Finally, just last month, Amazon reportedly narrowed its search to a small collection of actors, including Lowden, Turner, and Josh O'Connor (Challengers). Earlier in the process, everyone from Nicholas Hoult (Mad Max: Fury Road) to Dunkirk actor Harry Styles also tested. So, regardless of being allowed to audition or not, Cox faced some tough competition.
